A walkthrough of gate calls for anyone with a companion animal
What you should know comes first

Gate Calls for Companion Animal Travelers

Aurelia Skyways uses gate calls to keep boarding orderly and to reduce stress for animals and their handlers. When you are traveling with a companion animal, listen closely for your gate call, keep your documents ready, and stay near the assigned area once boarding begins. This helps staff move you smoothly and gives your animal a calmer transition to the aircraft.

The Companion Animal Travel Desk reviews each case before departure so the travel plan matches the species, temperament, and comfort needs of the animal. Keep your crate or carrier secure and your leash or restraint close at hand. If your animal needs a quiet approach, remain seated until staff invite you forward. A steady pace and brief movements usually make the process easier for everyone.

<<FACT F079>>

At the gate, follow staff direction without delay. If your companion animal is a bird, the combined weight of the animal and crate must meet the approved limit. <<FACT F065>> Keep the carrier closed unless a staff member asks you to open it, and never place the animal on a seat or on the floor outside the permitted area. If you are traveling with medication, food, or comfort items, keep them accessible in your carry-on bag.

Passengers with companion animals should arrive prepared for possible changes in boarding order. The team may adjust the sequence to protect animal welfare, manage space at the gate, or respond to operational needs. If your plans change, notify the desk as soon as possible so the staff can update the record and guide you to the right boarding point.

When the gate call is complete, proceed directly as instructed and keep your attention on the animal's comfort and safety. For more help, contact the Companion Animal Travel Desk before you travel or speak with staff at the gate.
